records.reason: m58 at 10/1 and 101.2 mg provides an intermediate point tied to the same-loading 50/1 observation 68a01853008546de06a1, whose completion was underestimated by 14.21 mL. The current 7.61/12.48 mL prediction tests where this phenol's weak-eluent growth begins; 39963f2ef0f22d86beed supplies additional, lower-loading 20/1 context.

m209 at 20/1 and 206.25 mg extends the exact loading and loading-solvent conditions of edfbbb86c05a0aeb1bfb at 5/1, measured at 7.45/17.05 mL. Together with the selected 50/1 point, it tests whether the current phenolic response grows smoothly or misses a sharper transition.

m209 at 50/1 completes the selected fixed-loading 5/1-observed, 20/1, 50/1 series. Its predicted 21.60/42.97 mL can discriminate persistent underprediction of donor-containing aromatics from a correctly learned slope, without assuming that m58's response transfers unchanged.

m108 at 50/1 and 100 mg extends the same-loading 20/1 observation 941f69aeb5995f34ea50. Recent positional isomer m122 observation b4877b0011db295949d5 finished at 26.39 mL at 50/1, whereas this row predicts 17.85 mL. Measuring m108 tests positional ether-response transfer; the isomer comparison has different loading amounts.

Trimethoxybenzene m110 at 50/1 predicts only 25.20 mL completion, compared with 22.00 mL measured at 20/1 in fea75df17d0bf593243f. This tests predicted weak-eluent flattening in a neutral multi-ether scaffold. The loading increases from 56.3 to 112.6 mg, so the comparison will inform joint condition effects rather than isolate solvent strength alone.

m190 at 10/1 fills the fixed-loading gap between 03e8372f11ac433be4fa at 1/1 and d1774335b45258bc173a at 20/1, with 7d9c7f40bc71ee7c4ef0 at 50/1. Its predicted onset of 10.99 mL exceeds the measured 20/1 onset of 7.57 mL. The label tests a possible onset maximum separately from completion growth.

m186 at 10/1 and 100 mg fills a fixed-loading response gap before 5f1ae4e354b8b36ec691 at 20/1 and 2efa93ea474f798b712a at 50/1. The current 10.26 mL onset is later than both measured weak-eluent onsets. This tests whether that local maximum is real and whether completion remains relatively modest.

m169 at 10/1 and 122 mg extends its same-condition-loading strong-eluent anchor 334348368030ba5ce3b6 at 1/1. The predicted 14.67/26.30 mL is substantially later than related chlorinated ketone m170 in b611d3bb1344a3e6a62a. The comparison tests transfer across chain length and ring fluorination, with those differences treated as hypotheses rather than established causes.

m169 at 50/1 pairs with its selected 10/1 point at identical loading and loading-solvent conditions. The model predicts a steep increase to 37.89/76.57 mL and places this row at the highest supplied CW-distance percentile. Two labels distinguish a genuine steep response from excessive transfer of retained-carbonyl features.

m172 at 50/1 extends the fixed-loading 10/1 observation c4b2566e6fe1d00b20ea, measured at 6.18/15.70 mL. The predicted 19.87/39.93 mL tests weak-eluent growth for a nonconjugated aryl/cyclopropyl ketone and helps locate where the strong response predicted for m169 does or does not generalize.

m196 at 50/1 and 155.2 mg extends 7a9ddf2102dcd051c2f7 at 5/1 with the same 700 uL loading-solvent volume. Its predicted 18.05/40.64 mL probes the unmeasured weak-eluent end of a brominated fused-ring aldehyde, providing a structural boundary for carbonyl response transfer.

m128 at 20/1 and 50 mg pairs with the selected 10/1, 50 mg row. Observation 92f7fe9d8581717a9949 established late elution at 10/1 and 100 mg, while related thioether aldehyde 4c46ceefd6147b1e0a7a was much earlier at 10/1. This fixed-loading pair tests whether the ketone's response flattens beyond 10/1.

The NH-containing enamine ester m72 at 10/1 and 51.1 mg extends the same-loading 5/1 observation cd638c08f0b730d298e8, measured at 14.61/31.20 mL. It establishes the transition before the selected 20/1 point and tests whether nitrogen-response features learned from pyridines transfer to a conjugated enamine.

m72 at 20/1 completes a fixed-loading 5/1-observed, 10/1, 20/1 series. The prediction reaches 31.22/67.67 mL with high CW distance. Measuring both new points discriminates a steep nitrogen-associated response from overextension of basic-ring features to this chemically different scaffold.

Ethyl nicotinate m90 at 2/1 and 55.35 mg fills an intermediate solvent regime missing from its measured 5/1 and 10/1 series, including b51b5dbcd2a38b174973 and 96710afeabc594baa359 at higher loading. The label tests whether pyridyl-ester retention rises early and how that transition depends on loading.

m19 at 2/1 and 46.1 mg provides the low-loading side of a matched pair around observed 304fb0fdb486ae4b7a07 at 92.2 mg, measured at 16.43/32.81 mL. The current low-loading prediction is 13.49/26.09 mL. This tests loading sensitivity in a tertiary-amine acrylate.

m19 at 2/1 and 138.3 mg completes the low, middle-observed, high-loading comparison while holding the loading solvent and its volume fixed. Its prediction is nearly identical to the selected 46.1 mg row. The pair can reveal suppressed endpoint-specific loading effects without imposing a universal mass correction.

m206 at 10/1 and 150 mg extends the steep hydroxymethylnaphthalene behavior measured at 5/1 in 614873124b33029a924c. Related hydroxyethylnaphthalene m205 was still later at 5/1 in 48853fd78c77153b963a. This tests donor connectivity and solvent-response transfer, acknowledging the loading difference from the measured m206 anchor.

m205 at 5/1 and 49.5 mg directly contrasts with 48853fd78c77153b963a at 99 mg under otherwise identical recorded conditions. The model predicts 52.30/97.83 mL, close to the measured higher-loading endpoints. The label tests whether a steep primary-alcohol scaffold preserves completion while onset responds to loading.

m103 at 2/1 and 303 mg directly contrasts with 640faac26ad46357bbbb at 202 mg, measured at 5.23/13.68 mL, with DCM and 600 uL loading-solvent volume fixed. Together with the selected 0/1, 202 mg row, it completes a two-eluent, two-loading rectangle and removes the confounding in the previous comparisons.

m103 at 0/1 and 202 mg contrasts with 1c2fe2551ccf2b35aacc at 303 mg, measured at 4.12/12.38 mL. This second missing corner of the loading-by-eluent rectangle can identify whether mass shifts onset and completion differently at 0/1 versus 2/1.

m13 at 2/1 and 168.3 mg extends the measured 56.1 and 112.2 mg points 74ce463c8423fbd22dc4 and 6573d8f84faaf7ce4a78. The current completion prediction of 14.94 mL is below both measured lower-loading completions. The label tests this loading extrapolation within a previously unstable multifunctional-carbonyl region.

m13 at 5/1 and 168.3 mg pairs with its selected 2/1 row and measured same-loading 10/1 record ca467c94f14b2219503e. Lower-loading 5/1 observations a421784c91de559c18e0 and 1cc3b837c6561b1c0a23 establish completion near 40–43 mL. This completes a response curve and tests whether the model's 38.50 mL completion is a loading effect or underfitting.

New dimethylbenzaldehyde m134 at 10/1 supplies the first point of a fixed-loading two-condition test. Related ortho-methyl aldehyde has measured 5/1 and 50/1 anchors 5070bf9690131f519648 and abb2d31b1372dbd64398. This row tests substitution-dependent carbonyl transfer without treating neighboring methyl substitution as interchangeable.

m134 at 50/1 pairs with its selected 10/1 row at 96.2 mg in PE with 300 uL loading-solvent volume. The model predicts modest growth from 6.86/15.84 to 7.33/20.39 mL. The pair determines whether the new scaffold follows this relatively flat curve or a steeper aldehyde response.

New dibromonaphthalene m5 at 50/1 probes a high-CW-distance hydrophobic structural gap. Bromonaphthalene observation ba5381d85ba24754040c and brominated fused-aromatic observation 42b3b7216aee53ebe1cc provide weak-eluent references with modest retention. The label tests whether the predicted 6.47/16.95 mL transfers across aromatic surface and halogen substitution.

m128 at 10/1 and 50 mg provides the matched-loading anchor for its selected 20/1 row and directly contrasts with 92f7fe9d8581717a9949 at 100 mg. It separates loading sensitivity from the subsequent solvent-response slope, making the two m128 labels a controlled local experiment.

New branched arylalkyl chloride m50 has low maximum similarity to measured molecules. At 10/1, its predicted 6.10/9.20 mL can be confronted with related linear chlorinated-chain observation 28767818a5e0052e4f5a. This tests structural transfer in the numerous early-eluting rows, where broad polar-family corrections should not dominate.

Cinnamic acid m173 at 0/1 uses 1500 uL loading solvent, near-matching the 2000 uL observation 6802f0b28c5a0c7b4c2a, whose completion was 50.30 mL. The loading amounts differ by only 0.05 mg. This tests whether unusually long strong-eluent completion persists across the recorded loading-solvent-volume change.

m173 at 1/1 pairs with the selected 0/1 row at identical 124.75 mg loading and 1500 uL loading-solvent volume. The model predicts completion falling from 47.77 to 17.42 mL despite weaker eluent. This pair discriminates a real unusual response from an extrapolation or record-specific anomaly; no mechanism is assumed.

Para-aminobenzonitrile m160 at 2/1 and 100 mg fills the exact-loading gap between fbf7711e24f45bf06d4f at 1/1 and b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90 at 5/1, where completion rises from 19.81 to 98.39 mL. It localizes this sharp transition and tests transfer from neutral nitrile features after adding an aniline donor.

Meta-aminobenzonitrile m161 at 2/1 and 100 mg forms a condition-matched positional comparison with the selected m160 row. Observations 0c24b9414856413c9a67 at 1/1 and 17902fa9c7f8ea9b456e at 5/1 anchor its own steep curve. The pair can teach positional nitrogen interactions while controlling loading and loading-solvent conditions.

hypotheses.content: Loading responses are scaffold- and eluent-dependent and can affect onset more than completion. The new m146 contrast supports this endpoint distinction, while the nearly flat m80 contrast and irregular nitrobenzophenone records rule out a universal strong loading correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Many supplied predictions barely change with loading. Controlled contrasts can teach conditional endpoint effects without converting historical anomalies into a global mass rule.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the completed m103 rectangle and m19 loading triplet reveal eluent-dependent completion shifts, and do m13, m128, and m205 preserve the onset/completion distinction?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl and neutral oxygenated-aromatic response curves depend on connectivity and substitution. Flat or modest beta-diketone behavior coexists with steep multifunctional ester and aldehyde curves; thioether ketone and aldehyde observations also differ substantially. A single polarity or carbonyl correction is insufficient.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local response curves can constrain where retained-carbonyl features transfer and where they cause excessive extrapolation or flattening. Structural comparisons also protect accurate low-retention families.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the steep m169 and m172 weak-eluent predictions real, and do m134, m196, m108, and m128 follow the response shapes predicted from their measured analogues?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing scaffolds have distinct solvent-response curves. Basic aromatic ring nitrogen shows steep retention, but pyridyl esters, tertiary-amine acrylates, and conjugated enamine esters cannot be assigned the same transition or loading response solely from nitrogen presence.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The large historical nitrogen-family errors motivate locating response transitions, while the now-accurate m146 completion contrast argues against applying another blanket upward correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does m90's response rise between strong and intermediate eluent, and does m72 retain the steep weak-eluent growth predicted from other nitrogen-containing scaffolds?

hypotheses.content: The recorded volume of loading solvent can affect endpoints in a scaffold-dependent way, as shown by m125. This is distinct from changing sample V/ul, which also changes density-times-volume loading amount. The m80 comparison does not isolate loading-solvent-volume effects. The unusually long strong-eluent completion of m173 remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Correctly separating the two recorded volume variables avoids attributing loading effects to injection-solvent volume. The acid pair tests an unusual completion pattern under explicitly controlled recorded conditions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m173 preserve long completion at 0/1 when loading-solvent volume decreases from 2000 to 1500 uL, and is its predicted completion decrease at 1/1 observed at fixed volume?

hypotheses.content: The corrected modest, substitution-specific response of neutral aryl nitriles should remain distinct from amino-substituted nitriles. Recent m130 and m144 labels support the neutral-nitrile correction, while measured amino-nitrile labels show much later completion at 5/1. Their intermediate-eluent transition is incompletely resolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The paired amino-nitrile measurements test a functional-group interaction boundary while avoiding renewed overcorrection of neutral nitriles whose recent predictions were much closer.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At identical 2/1 conditions, do meta- and para-aminobenzonitrile have similar transition points or materially different endpoint responses?

hypotheses.content: Phenols and ortho-hydroxyaldehydes have scaffold-specific weak-eluent responses, including different onset and completion behavior. Recent m58 and m209 labels exposed underprediction, whereas m197 at 20/1 showed substantial completion with an earlier onset than predicted. Positional substitution or intramolecular interactions are possible explanations, but the observations do not establish those mechanisms.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These labels can teach donor-by-structure solvent interactions and distinguish delayed completion from uniformly delayed onset. They also limit overgeneralization of the earlier ortho-hydroxyaldehyde anomaly.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m186 and m190 really have onset maxima around 10/1, and do the m58 and m209 extensions reveal smooth growth or sharper solvent-response transitions?

hypotheses.content: Large single-predictor quantile spans and large CW distance were hypothesized to preferentially reveal useful model failures. The latest outcomes support some coverage gaps but weaken their reliability as standalone acquisition signals.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Exploration remains useful when a candidate tests a plausible structural transfer gap, but broad spans alone should not consume the batch. The supplied onset spans are especially difficult to interpret because q10 values are zero and some quantiles cross.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the new dibromonaphthalene and branched arylalkyl chloride labels expose transferable structural errors despite the recent accuracy of several unfamiliar low-polarity rows?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes shift emphasis from broad width-based exploration toward controlled response tests. m58 completion was underestimated by 14.21 mL at 50/1, m122 by 7.71 mL at 50/1, and m209 by 6.33 mL at 5/1, strengthening scaffold-specific oxygen/donor follow-up. In contrast, iodothiophene, a simple aryl bromide, chloroiodobenzene, and m170 were close to their acquisition-time predictions, weakening the claim that unfamiliar or broad-span rows reliably imply large error. The m146 loading change from 108.3 to 162.45 mg advanced onset by 1.70 mL while completion increased by only 0.89 mL, supporting endpoint-specific loading effects. The m80 change from 50 to 100 uL sample V shifted both endpoints by only about 0.1 mL; its loading-solvent volume stayed at 200 uL, so it neither demonstrates an injection-solvent-volume effect nor supports a universal strong mass response. I also correct the previous m103 loading description: the measured amounts were 202 and 303 mg, not 100 and 150 mg. Its prior comparisons changed eluent and loading together, motivating the missing rectangle corners. Recent m130 and m144 outcomes support the corrected modest neutral-nitrile response, so the next nitrile measurements target the amino-substitution boundary. m197 at 20/1 finished at 37.24 mL, close to its prior completion prediction, while onset was earlier; this narrows the earlier ortho-hydroxyaldehyde hypothesis to scaffold- and endpoint-specific behavior rather than a universal anomalous curve.
batch_rationale: The batch uses the supplied pool to answer linked learning questions. The m103 rectangle, m19 triplet around a measured middle loading, and m13 extensions separate loading effects from solvent-response curvature. The m128 pair adds a fixed-loading slope test plus a direct loading contrast with its measured 10/1 anchor. The m72 series and matched amino-nitrile isomers locate unresolved nitrogen-associated transitions, while m90 probes a pyridyl-ester boundary. Phenol and hydroxyaldehyde follow-up targets recent failures without assuming that all donors require the same correction. m169 receives two fixed-condition-loading points because its predicted steep curve is insufficiently anchored; m172 and m196 test related carbonyl transfer boundaries. Neutral ethers and the naphthyl alcohol rows examine whether learned features transfer across oxygen connectivity. The m173 pair tests an unusual predicted inverse completion response and a recorded loading-solvent-volume extension, leaving its mechanism open. New m134 receives a meaningful two-point curve, while m5 and m50 provide targeted early-eluting structural coverage. These labels may improve Row-distribution accuracy by teaching conditional relationships and limiting both excessive extrapolation and over-flattening. Historical acquisition errors guide failure repair but are not treated as current residuals; elution interval width is treated as a measured endpoint relationship, separately from the predictor's quantile spans.
